messages:
Aisha (support): FYI - customer 'Acme' opened a ticket: streaming responses from /v1/stream drop after ~30-45s. Client sees a few partial events then connection closes. They get a socket write error in their client logs (EPIPE / EAGAIN) and our side shows a runtime write failure followed by an abort. They also complain about doubled output and unexpected billing for overlapping tokens.

Sam W (eng-runtime): Thanks — do we know whether they go through a proxy (nginx/cloudfront) or direct to hosted endpoints? Any sample request/headers?

Aisha (support): Hosted API, behind their corporate reverse-proxy and also CloudFront in front of ours. They pasted their snippet; using text/event-stream SSE. Quick curl they ran: `curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-rx\"` then piping to a slow consumer (`pv -qL 20`) causes the problem. They saw repeated lines: 'write error: Broken pipe' and then our runtime logs show: `write to client failed: send: resource temporarily unavailable (EAGAIN)`, then `connection aborted by runtime`.

Ingrid (eng-sre): This sounds classic slow-consumer/backpressure. If the client's read loop is throttled (pv -qL), the kernel send buffer fills -> send returns EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK; if we aren't handling backpressure at the application layer we end up queueing up many response bytes in user-land, then runtime eventually aborts the connection. Does our proxy in front have proxy_buffering on? Nginx default buffering will happily accept upstream data and buffer it, which masks backpressure until the proxy's buffer limit is hit, then it returns 502/504.

Miguel (eng-oncall): Repro steps I used locally: \n```
# simulate slow consumer and reproduce EAGAIN
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 'https://localhost:8443/v1/stream?model=gpt-rx' | pv -qL 10
```
After ~20-40s the client side shows 'Broken pipe' and server logs include: `runtime: write error: Broken pipe (EPIPE)` followed by `runtime: aborting stream id=... reason=slow_consumer`.

Sam W (eng-runtime): Helpful. Two immediate axes: client fixes and server-side mitigations. Client side: make sure consumer reads the stream continuously (not batching reads), increase socket recv buffer, or implement internal buffering for the stream. Example Node snippet to ensure drain loop doesn't block: \n```
// simple node streaming consumer
const res = await fetch(url, opts);
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  // process quickly and yield back to event loop
  processChunk(value);
}
```
If the customer is doing heavy sync processing per chunk, that will block the read loop. Recommend offloading heavy work to a worker and keep read path tight.

Ingrid (eng-sre): Server-side short-term mitigations for hosted customers:
- Ensure upstream/proxy has `proxy_buffering off;` and `proxy_read_timeout` bumped to 300s for streaming routes.
- Send periodic keepalive SSE comments (":\n") every 10-15s to keep proxies and NAT alive.
- Implement small server-side backpressure limits: if per-connection pending bytes > 256KB, apply backpressure signals to the generator (pause model token emission) and if client doesn't catch up within configurable timeout (eg 60s) close connection gracefully with a `retry-after` style event.

Aisha (support): Customer asked about billing — why are tokens duplicated when they reconnect?

Sam W (eng-runtime): Two causes we've seen: (1) if client reconnects and the server resumes by re-sending the last window of tokens (no dedupe id), the client sees overlapping tokens and those bytes were produced (billed) twice on our side; (2) if a generator kept producing while the socket was backed up and the connection is aborted, our accounting sometimes counted tokens at generation time rather than final delivery. Short term we can: attach chunk ids to SSE events and include `last_chunk_id` in reconnect requests so server dedupes; longer term we should move to 'token-finalize-on-ack' accounting or mark dupe tokens as reversible credits in edge cases.

Miguel (eng-oncall): Short actionable checklist I pushed to the ticket for the customer:
- Turn off nginx proxy_buffering for their route: `location /v1/stream { proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 3600s; }`
- If they can't change proxy: have client add occasional reads/keepalive to avoid long pauses, or increase recv buffer and read speed.
- Use curl repro above and attach both client PV output and server logs.

Sam W (eng-runtime): Additional useful repro: run a producer that ignores backpressure to show how resource usage grows: \n```
# producer simply generates tokens regardless of socket state
for i in $(seq 1 100000); do printf 'data: token-%s\n\n' \"$i\"; sleep 0.01; done
```
Then throttle the consumer with `pv -qL 5` and watch `ss -tin` and kernel transmit queue growth, and then server EAGAIN.

Aisha (support): Customer applied proxy_buffering off and keepalives; they still saw a drop but much later (5-7min). They want a robust server-side knob we can toggle for hosted accounts.

Sam W (eng-runtime): I'll open a small runtime change: add config `slow_consumer_threshold_bytes` (default 262144) and `slow_consumer_timeout_s` (default 60). If threshold exceeded the runtime will pause token generation (when supported by model runner) and emit a SSE comment ' :paused\n' every 5s. If not recovered by timeout, emit an event `event: stream_closed\ndata: {"reason":"slow_consumer"}\n\n` and terminate. This avoids runaway memory vs abrupt EPIPE and gives client a clear code path.

Ingrid (eng-sre): Also recommend we add observability: per-connection pending_bytes metric, count of slow_consumer terminations, and an alert when rate rises in hosted fleet.

Miguel (eng-oncall): Action items:
- Sam: PR for threshold + SSE pause behavior (P1 backlog for runtime)
- Ingrid: dashboard for pending_bytes + alert (P2)
- Support: advise customers to disable proxy buffering and add keepalives; share curls and node snippet.

Aisha (support): Thanks — I updated the ticket with the repro commands and temporary mitigations. Reassigning to Sam for runtime follow-up. :thumbsup:
